graham.brief:
The 42.5 total and the spread leave Tennessee only about 15.5 points to score. Even so, Cam Ward is set at 33.5 pass attempts, over his 29.3 average across three games.

Look first at Ward's recent workload. Ward's pass attempts climbed from 20 to 36 last week. A role like that would make Ward's early games the wrong baseline. As the underdog, Tennessee could be throwing more once the fourth quarter arrives.

Three games of Ward can point somewhere without proving anything. So which one describes Sunday for Ward, his recent workload or the low Tennessee point total? If Tennessee leans on Ward from the start, the line looks right, and if not, his average does. Watch the early-down Tennessee calls, because that's where Ward's volume starts.
